learning_outcomes.text: Knows the operating principles of microprocessors and microcontrollers used in mechatronic applications.
Understands the architectural differences between types of processors (von Neumann, Harvard, CISC, RISC).
Knows low and medium-level programming languages used in embedded application development.
Understands the hardware and software structure of development platforms like Arduino and 8051.
Applies data conversion and acquisition methods (ADC, DAC) and integrates them into demonstrative applications.
Develops applications with serial communications (UART, SPI, I2C) and PWM control for mechatronic systems.
Integrates input/output, timing, and digital display modules into functional applications.
Demonstrates responsibility in using hardware and software platforms in the laboratory.
Develops clear technical documentation for projects developed with microcontrollers.
Shows autonomy in designing and testing embedded solutions specific to intelligent systems.
Takes an active role in developing robust autonomous applications for Mechanical Engineering.

syllabus_topics: Use of binary and hexadecimal operating system, Conversions from decimal to binary and hexadecimal systems, Performing logical-arithmetic operations in hexadecimal system

Presentation of main differences between microprocessors, microcontrollers, CISC, RISC, von Neumann and Harvard architectures; Increasing microprocessor performance by using an extended set of register locations, pipelining technique, and cache memory; Advantages of microcontrollers from the perspective of hardware resources on the same integrated circuit; Fast signal processing processors

Description of the general architecture of an Intel-type microprocessor system; comparisons between Intel, AMD, and Motorola Power PC processors; General presentation of the Intel x86 microprocessor and the Motorola Power PC microprocessor; Methods for testing the computational performance of microprocessors from various families using benchmark tests
Generalities regarding microprocessor languages; Instruction encoding; Example of a restricted machine code type language

Arithmetic, logical, boolean, branching (jump) and data transfer instructions; Arithmetic instructions: addition, subtraction, multiplication and division in single and double precision; Logical instructions - AND, OR, Exclusive OR, Complement, 2's Complement; Boolean instructions (bit-level) - AND, OR, NOT, shifts, rotations; Conditional or unconditional jump instructions

Memories and addressing modes used in microprocessors and microcontrollers; RAM, ROM, EEPROM and Flash memories, Data memories and Program memories; Addressing modes: inter-register, direct, immediate, indirect, absolute, indexed, between memory blocks
Basic architecture of the ARDUINO development system; Programming; Input/Output Interfaces; Development Kit
Writing a C program in Arduino 1.8 Platform
Execution of demonstrative programs from the ARDUINO application library
Execution of examples for creating demonstrative applications using the C programming language in ARDUINO

Analog-to-digital and digital-to-analog conversion techniques; converters and data acquisition experimented with the ARDUINO Kit; Notions regarding conversion resolution and acquisition speed; Parallel, serial A/D and D/A conversion techniques, with weighted resistive networks, sigma-delta
Presentation of hardware and software aspects of I/O transfer techniques

Operation and programming of a Timer/Counter module; Methods for measuring the period and frequency of signals with applications in the automotive industry; Emitting pulse trains with variable PWM duty cycle
Inter-processor connection and communications using serial link, I2C, SPI
Presentation of Arduino Kit 1, Assembly of the workbench; Presentation of the Arduino Software IDE development platform; Presentation of C instructions from the Arduino CC Library with examples
Execution of LED Blinking circuit on a prototype board and execution of the program for turning on/off an LED at various frequencies; Control of a 7-segment display using Arduino Uno Kit

Development of a serial communication program between a Windows PC and an Arduino Kit by sending and receiving messages between the two entities; Hardware/software development of a digital display system using an Arduino Uno kit and a 2x16 alphanumeric display
Development of a digital voltmeter using the Arduino Uno kit; Study of the significance of PWM control using an RGB LED coupled to the Arduino Uno kit

Control of a DC motor using the Arduino Uno kit; Presentation and control of a digitally actuated servomechanism via Arduino-Uno kit; Hardware/software implementation of a digital Thermometer and Hygrometer using Arduino Kit
Presentation of a Robot using the Arduino Robot Starter Kit
Project submission
teaching_methods: Short recap of previous course notions
Use of video projector and whiteboard for demonstrations
Discussion of technical solutions and causes of failures
Presentation of Arduino Robot Starter Kit
Presentation of how to build an electronic circuit using a prototype board, electronic components, pin wires, and Starter Kit

assessment_methods.method: Ongoing observation, individual/team assignments, case study reports

assessment_rules: The final evaluation result for a discipline is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity. Whole grades from 10 to 1 will be awarded, with grade 5 certifying the acquisition of minimal learning outcomes and corresponding study credits. A minimum grade of 5 is required for the Colloquium/Verification and for the Project.
